title: Ants on a Triangle
problem: An ant stands at each vertex of a triangle. Simultaneously, each independently chooses one of the two directions around the triangle with equal probability and walks to the next vertex. What is the probability that no two ants collide?

hints.text: A collision is avoided only if all ants choose a consistent direction around the triangle.
There are 2^3 direction choices and two safe choices: all clockwise or all counterclockwise.

solution.setup: Encode each ant's choice as clockwise or counterclockwise.
solution.reasoning: There are eight equally likely direction triples. If all go clockwise or all go counterclockwise, they rotate without collision. Any mixed choice sends two ants toward the same edge or vertex. Thus two outcomes are safe.
solution.sanityCheck: The two safe outcomes are symmetric and each has probability (1/2)^3=1/8.

keyInsight: Characterize globally collision-free motion before counting local direction choices.
recognitionCues: Symmetric agents make independent binary choices on a cycle.
commonMistakes: Assuming each pair avoids collision independently.
followUps: Generalize to n ants on an n-gon.

source.notes: Original wording of a classic directional puzzle.

verification.notes: Only the two unanimous directions are safe.
